selectionRule: Choose one primary type by the reader's intended outcome, not the topic, size, HTML components or the word research alone.

sectionRules.required: Required semantic coverage belongs under at most five main h2 groups, using h3/h4 subsections. It may be merged, never silently dropped.
sectionRules.recommended: Include when it helps the reader reach the selected outcome. Omit rather than fill with generic prose.
sectionRules.conditional: Include only when its stated condition applies; an explicit user request can make it required.
sectionRules.unknowns: State evidence, ownership, capacity, dates and baselines as unknown or proposed when unverified. Never invent values to fill a section.
sectionRules.sources: Ground claims in actually read sources and preserve meaningful limits. Respect explicit reader-facing citation restrictions without inventing attribution.
sectionRules.authority: A document, selected option or readiness control never approves investment, publication, release or external actions.
sectionRules.advanced: Use progressive details for advanced scenarios and references. Never collapse material qualifications out of the overview.

types.name: Research and investigation
types.goal: Explain what the evidence establishes and what remains unknown.
types.outcome: The reader can understand the subject, distinguish fact from inference and identify the limits of the answer.
useWhen: Compare documented approaches without requesting a decision

required.title: Topic, questions and scope
required.purpose: Identify the exact questions and material version/environment boundaries.

required.title: Terminology
required.purpose: Define the actual terms, distinctions and scope limits needed to understand this paper; do not imply agreement or implementation from a definition.

required.title: Summary of findings
required.purpose: Answer the questions concisely without substituting a proposal.

required.title: Method and source coverage
required.purpose: State what was inspected or actually tested and what was not.

required.title: Findings and explanations
required.purpose: Support findings near their claims; separate observation, reporting and inference.

required.title: Limitations and open questions
required.purpose: Retain contrary evidence, gaps and scope limits that affect interpretation.

required.title: Conclusion
required.purpose: Resolve what is known and unknown without forcing an action.

required.title: Sources and references
required.purpose: Provide actual source provenance and relevant evidence boundaries.

recommended.title: Concepts and background
recommended.purpose: Explain only concepts needed to follow the findings.

recommended.title: Comparison or worked example
recommended.purpose: Make differences understandable without fabricating measurements.

conditional.title: Requested recommendations or implications
conditional.when: The user explicitly asks for recommendations, implications or next steps.
conditional.purpose: Keep requested advice separate from informational findings.

outcomeChecks: Every requested question is answered or explicitly unresolved.
Claims have evidence and relevant limits.
No invented problem, urgency, funding ask or default recommendation.
No more than five major sections; terminology and reader-persona controls are present.
Advanced references are collapsible, while decisive conclusions and critical qualifications remain visible.

types.name: Product vision
types.goal: Align teams on the product promise and the future user experience.
types.outcome: The reader understands who benefits, what changes, the shared foundation and the direction to endorse.
useWhen: Describe a future experience without writing an implementation specification

required.title: Problem statement and context
required.purpose: Name the affected user task, current gap and consequence.

required.title: Terminology
required.purpose: Define the actual terms, distinctions and scope limits needed to understand this paper; do not imply agreement or implementation from a definition.

required.title: TLDR of the proposal
required.purpose: State the direction, benefit, reuse boundary and requested alignment.

required.title: Product promise and future experience
required.purpose: Describe the changed user journey and why it matters.

required.title: Personas and concrete scenario
required.purpose: Show relevant user needs through a plausible, labelled scenario.

required.title: Shared foundation and boundaries
required.purpose: Explain common capabilities, ownership/reuse and what is not promised.

required.title: First proof and decision
required.purpose: Separate the bounded first slice from ambition; state what to endorse and prove.

required.title: Sources and evidence boundaries
required.purpose: Distinguish source-backed context, proposed experience and unresolved choices.

required.title: Direction decision requested
required.purpose: State the product direction and bounded proof to endorse, with unresolved commitments visible.

recommended.title: Alternatives and platform advantage
recommended.purpose: Explain why this direction beats the strongest alternative.

recommended.title: Measures of user value
recommended.purpose: Define outcomes without inventing baselines or targets.

recommended.title: Evolution of the experience
recommended.purpose: Show expansion without presenting a delivery schedule as committed.

conditional.title: Architecture reference
conditional.when: A separate implementation paper exists and technical detail would distract here.
conditional.purpose: Refer to verified architecture by name/link; do not duplicate its full build inventory.

outcomeChecks: A reader can describe the intended experience and its value.
The bounded first proof and future ambition are distinct.
The direction is proposed, not invented team agreement or delivered capability.
No more than five major sections; terminology and reader-persona controls are present.
Advanced references are collapsible, while decisive conclusions and critical qualifications remain visible.

types.name: Strategy and investment
types.goal: Choose what to fund, stop, defer or consolidate.
types.outcome: The decision maker can accept a concrete investment and its tradeoff, or choose the condition for not proceeding.
useWhen: Decide which parallel work to stop or converge

required.title: Problem statement and context
required.purpose: Establish the evidenced task failure and why a direction change is needed.

required.title: Terminology
required.purpose: Define the actual terms, distinctions and scope limits needed to understand this paper; do not imply agreement or implementation from a definition.

required.title: TLDR of the proposal
required.purpose: State the recommended investment and reuse/containment boundary.

required.title: Strategic choice and alternatives
required.purpose: Compare real options, including the strongest alternative and cost of doing nothing.

required.title: Investment boundary and tradeoffs
required.purpose: State scope, resources/ownership to confirm, what stops and what remains available.

required.title: First proof and success/stop criteria
required.purpose: Define the smallest evidence-based slice and what changes the recommendation.

required.title: Decision requested
required.purpose: Name the bounded choice, accountable decision role and next action.

required.title: Sources and evidence boundaries
required.purpose: Keep claims, assumptions and meaningful uncertainties inspectable.

recommended.title: Current state and constraints
recommended.purpose: Add maturity or capability context that materially changes the choice.

recommended.title: Phased investment
recommended.purpose: Stage funding around proof rather than invent a full roadmap.

recommended.title: Ownership beyond the author
recommended.purpose: Explain how the investment avoids recurring dependency on one person.

conditional.title: Cost or capacity model
conditional.when: Comparable inputs are available or the user requests a clearly labelled model.
conditional.purpose: Expose assumptions; do not manufacture financial or staffing facts.

outcomeChecks: One actual choice and its strongest alternative are explicit.
Scope, resource uncertainty and stop conditions are visible.
The ask enables an investment decision rather than a generic vision endorsement.
No more than five major sections; terminology and reader-persona controls are present.
Advanced references are collapsible, while decisive conclusions and critical qualifications remain visible.

types.name: Architecture and convergence
types.goal: Adopt shared contracts and migrate without losing intended behavior.
types.outcome: Implementers know the chosen interfaces, ownership/reuse boundaries and proof needed to converge safely.
useWhen: Decide a shared contract or service boundary

required.title: Problem statement and context
required.purpose: Show the flow that breaks or diverges and the behavior to preserve.

required.title: Terminology
required.purpose: Define the actual terms, distinctions and scope limits needed to understand this paper; do not imply agreement or implementation from a definition.

required.title: TLDR of the proposal
required.purpose: State the contract/reuse choice and smallest missing extension.

required.title: Contracts and responsibilities
required.purpose: Identify producers, consumers, ownership, standards/status and relevant failure/authority semantics.

required.title: Reuse and alternatives
required.purpose: Justify direct reuse, adapters or a new boundary against the strongest alternative.

required.title: Migration and proof
required.purpose: State compatibility, conformance, rollout/rollback and retirement conditions.

required.title: Decision requested
required.purpose: Name what interface/boundary is adopted and who owns the next proof.

required.title: Sources and evidence boundaries
required.purpose: Distinguish standards, verified behavior, proposals and coverage gaps.

recommended.title: Component build map and inventory
recommended.purpose: Connect logical code units and dependencies without implying one service per box.

recommended.title: Worked data or lifecycle flow
recommended.purpose: Make authored inputs, processing, retained records and outputs concrete.

recommended.title: Operational and access boundaries
recommended.purpose: Explain material reliability, identity, privacy and resource constraints.

conditional.title: Complete implementation inventory
conditional.when: The user explicitly requests every component or a full build map.
conditional.purpose: Include every known code area, dependency, build/reuse distinction and unresolved deployment boundary.

conditional.title: API or command reference
conditional.when: Interfaces are needed to understand or implement the requested boundary.
conditional.purpose: Label proposed contracts and keep examples source-grounded.

outcomeChecks: The shared contract and compatibility meaning are explicit.
Required code/ownership boundaries are understood without reading between boxes.
Migration proof and the anti-duplication/retirement choice are actionable.
No more than five major sections; terminology and reader-persona controls are present.
Advanced references are collapsible, while decisive conclusions and critical qualifications remain visible.

types.name: Evidence and recommendation
types.goal: Decide whether to proceed, narrow, stop or collect a specific missing proof.
types.outcome: The decision owner can take a bounded action justified by the evidence and understands what it does not authorize.
useWhen: Recommend next steps from a spike
Resolve a go/no-go choice blocked by uncertainty

required.title: Decision blocked and context
required.purpose: Name the uncertainty, representative scenario and consequence of acting on it.

required.title: Terminology
required.purpose: Define the actual terms, distinctions and scope limits needed to understand this paper; do not imply agreement or implementation from a definition.

required.title: TLDR of the recommendation
required.purpose: State proceed/narrow/stop/collect proof and the condition that changes it.

required.title: Method and evidence boundaries
required.purpose: State what was actually inspected or tested and what was not.

required.title: Findings that change the decision
required.purpose: Connect each decisive finding to evidence, limitation and consequence.

required.title: Recommendation and next proof
required.purpose: State the smallest action/test, success/stop criteria and ownership to confirm.

required.title: Decision requested
required.purpose: Resolve the bounded choice without turning the draft into approval.

required.title: Sources and limitations
required.purpose: Retain contrary evidence, unresolved uncertainty and original provenance.

recommended.title: Matched comparison or finding matrix
recommended.purpose: Hold relevant inputs constant and expose incompatible comparisons.

recommended.title: What remains available
recommended.purpose: Protect existing behavior until replacement proof exists.

conditional.title: Reproduction or test detail
conditional.when: An actual test was performed and the detail helps verify the conclusion.
conditional.purpose: Do not write a planned experiment as an executed result.

outcomeChecks: The recommendation follows from decisive evidence, not the desired answer.
Limits and contrary findings can change the choice.
The next action is bounded and separate from broad investment or release authority.
No more than five major sections; terminology and reader-persona controls are present.
Advanced references are collapsible, while decisive conclusions and critical qualifications remain visible.

types.name: Delivery roadmap
types.goal: Sequence delivery against explicit targets, dependencies and readiness gates.
types.outcome: Owners can commit or revise a coherent delivery slice and see how scope or dependency changes threaten the targets.
useWhen: Set first shipment, GA and launch targets
Sequence work packages and integration coverage

required.title: Outcome, scope and current gap
required.purpose: Explain the user journey to deliver and distinguish confirmed capability from planned work.

required.title: Terminology
required.purpose: Define the actual terms, distinctions and scope limits needed to understand this paper; do not imply agreement or implementation from a definition.

required.title: TLDR of the delivery plan
required.purpose: State target releases, scope/reuse boundary and the commitment to request.

required.title: Release targets and phases
required.purpose: Retain user-supplied dates, distinguish planning anchors from verified event dates and define each release's scope.

required.title: Work packages and dependencies
required.purpose: Map deliverables, prerequisite relationships and acceptance proof, not a disconnected feature wish list.

required.title: Readiness gates and delivery risk
required.purpose: Keep targets fixed when modeling delay; identify evidence required to expand, hold or rebaseline.

required.title: Ownership, capacity and assumptions
required.purpose: Name proposed/confirmed accountable roles, unassigned capacity and unresolved external dependencies.

required.title: Delivery decision requested
required.purpose: Ask for scope/ownership/capacity or an explicit rebaseline, not pretend the plan is funded.

required.title: Sources and planning boundaries
required.purpose: Ground scope in vision/architecture and preserve uncertainty about estimates, dates and readiness.

recommended.title: Monthly delivery view
recommended.purpose: Expose the complete horizon and concrete monthly outcomes.

recommended.title: Tool or audience coverage matrix
recommended.purpose: Define the denominator behind full support and required journeys.

recommended.title: Dependency what-if model
recommended.purpose: Show deterministic propagation without claiming an effort or staffing forecast.

recommended.title: Launch and operating handoff
recommended.purpose: Plan support, rollback and sustained ownership after shipment.

conditional.title: Complete requested horizon
conditional.when: The user specifies a horizon or monthly plan.
conditional.purpose: Include every requested period; don't replace a full roadmap with three milestone cards.

conditional.title: Full support definition
conditional.when: The user asks for all tools, surfaces or components.
conditional.purpose: List the planning catalog, validation gate and compatibility bar rather than redefine all implicitly.

outcomeChecks: Each target has scope, dependencies and required proof.
Every requested period and explicit coverage target is represented.
Ownership/capacity and event-date uncertainty are visible; simulations never approve or deploy.
No more than five major sections; terminology and reader-persona controls are present.
Advanced references are collapsible, while decisive conclusions and critical qualifications remain visible.

mainSections.title: Release targets and complete delivery view

types.name: Adoption and operating model
types.goal: Turn an agreed capability into repeated user value and durable ownership.
types.outcome: The reader knows how users reach value, how it is measured and who runs routine operation without the author as a dependency.
useWhen: Improve adoption or a user journey
Define operating ownership and a sustainable handoff

required.title: Adoption problem and context
required.purpose: Identify the actual journey bottleneck, cohort and repeated manual dependency.

required.title: Terminology
required.purpose: Define the actual terms, distinctions and scope limits needed to understand this paper; do not imply agreement or implementation from a definition.

required.title: TLDR of the operating proposal
required.purpose: State the adoption intervention, reuse choice and operating decision.

required.title: Journey and measurement
required.purpose: Define user completion, outcome denominator, available signals and unconfirmed baseline/targets.

required.title: Ownership that lasts
required.purpose: Define accountable owner/deputy, routine decisions, support/escalation and handoff proof.

required.title: Rollout and operating proof
required.purpose: State cohort, expansion/stop conditions and how repeated value/independence will be demonstrated.

required.title: Operating decision requested
required.purpose: Resolve the ownership or adoption action and what remains with the decision owner.

required.title: Sources and evidence boundaries
required.purpose: Ground user friction and measurement limits without inventing adoption or delegation success.

recommended.title: Persona or cohort journey
recommended.purpose: Show different adoption needs without changing shared outcome meaning.

recommended.title: Support and feedback loop
recommended.purpose: Make recurring diagnosis, exception handling and improvement sustainable.

recommended.title: Coverage and exceptions
recommended.purpose: Identify included users/tools and deliberate exceptions.

conditional.title: Author step-back test
conditional.when: Removing routine dependence on the author is a stated objective.
conditional.purpose: Define a verifiable handoff period and escalation boundary, not claim a handoff already happened.

outcomeChecks: Success is a completed/repeated user journey, not just reach or installs.
Routine operation has accountable ownership and a concrete independence proof.
Expansion and exceptions use evidence rather than assumed adoption.
No more than five major sections; terminology and reader-persona controls are present.
Advanced references are collapsible, while decisive conclusions and critical qualifications remain visible.
